newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's future leader seeks chef.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's future leader seeks chef.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader may be dissatisfied with many aspects of his dealings with the outgoing colonial government but he cannot complain it is ignoring his creature comforts.

The colonial civil service has advertised for a chef to serve the Chief Executive, Tung Chee-hwa, who takes over from Governor Chris Patten when the British furl their flag and depart at midnight on June 30, 1997.

The candidate must be able to cook Chinese cuisine, specifically Cantonese or Shanghainese, be fluent in the Cantonese dialect spoken in Hong Kong, be prepared to work irregular hours and wear a uniform, the advertisement, carried in weekend newspapers, said.
The upside -- housing goes with the job, which is not to be sniffed at in high-rent Hong Kong.
The salary ranges from HK$16,050-18,595 (US$2,057-2,400) a month.
